user.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
The book shelf is a small local web app with no accounts. It stores books in `data/books.json`, so they are still there after a restart.

Open it with `npm start`, then go to http://127.0.0.1:3000. The home page lists what you are currently reading and what you have finished. The form adds a book with a title, an author, and notes. Each title links to its own page, and that address is the link you can send. Mark finished is on the shelf and on the book page.

`npm test` passed, exit code 0, 4 tests. A live check also added a book, opened its link, marked it finished, and confirmed the JSON file updated.

The server only listens on this machine. To share a link with someone on your network, start it with `HOST=0.0.0.0 npm start` and send them the book URL shown on the page.

{"action":"run","command":"set -e
curl -sS -o /tmp/home.html -w 'home:%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3000/
grep -o 'Currently reading\|Finished\|Add a book' /tmp/home.html
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/books \
  --data-urlencode 'title=Kindred' \
  --data-urlencode 'author=Octavia Butler' \
  --data-urlencode 'notes=Time and place'
echo '--- json ---'
cat /tmp/books-smoke.json
echo
LOC=$(python3 -c 'import json; print("/books/"+json.load(open("/tmp/books-smoke.json"))[0]["id"])')
echo "link:$LOC"
curl -sS -o /tmp/book.html -w 'book:%{http_code}\n' "http://127.0.0.1:3000$LOC"
grep -o 'Kindred\|Octavia Butler\|Time and place\|Send this link' /tmp/book.html
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000$LOC/finish" --data 'next=/'
echo '--- after finish ---'
python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("/tmp/books-smoke.json"))[0]["status"])'
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:3000/ | python3 -c 'import sys; html=sys.stdin.read(); r=html.split("id=\"finished\"",1)[0]; f=html.split("id=\"finished\"",1)[1]; print("reading has Kindred", "Kindred" in r); print("finished has Kindred", "Kindred" in f)'"}
